79161523.title: File:Blue Danube (Exercise and variations-collections in piano) JMC, Han.ogg

ImageDescription.value:
To make this sound image of Blue Danube in piano (Collections of some variations for annually continuing exercises), my thinking is like:

1. Originally, its notation wasn't from piano but orchestration (In my world, I never saw or heard any pianists play it). 2. However, its beauties have been shared annually and wordwidely year by year. 3. Piano's solo-style should also accept aesthetic appreciation of Vienna School, especially this beautiful melody, deeply in heart, which from my earlier education was heard, till today. So long the time was, and why didn't I practice some? Evenly never a chance to the stage, in classroom and with some my students (Next generations rather than me), I think I should give my thanks to the Era. 4. Indeed, it's long time that I find Sir Chopin's many 'Independent fingering' techniques of waltz have been applied into this melody, especially left hand's accompaniment. Therefore, I think the training of it would help me improve my hands' controllability. 5. It can also motive my piano education (teaching and learning) to a higher level, in which we can try to realize some impossible & challenge points, such as solo for a band (just a try), and the long-distance flying of left hand as the accompaniment. 6. I will get a chance travelling in Vienna and right alongside the 'Blue Danube' - one of my dreamland from childhood. Though I have no-too-much money (myself), I thought the exercises of Blue Danube (though time is always limited for me, I would play it for long and submit different editions time after time), as a gift from a piano teacher's own heart, would be in romantic. 7. I heard: in this year's Vienna New Year's Concert in 'Golden Hall', Germany 'Big Bear' conductor used it as the exercises for the band in every time before the rehearsal. I thought why not in piano classroom? Therefore, though its length is in a huge paragraph and currently it was heard rough, I picked up some important variations for the piano exercises, which looks like a whole melody. Hopefully, someday I can get a total edition (heard mostly like) for performance.

In addition, could you hear its magic power - a small unknown bird was always attempting to follow the melody in this sound image...

Artist.value: Jason M. C., Han

80317990.title: File:Cole Porter’s “I Love You” - JMC, Han's Piano Edition.ogg

ImageDescription.value:
Cole Porter's I Love You was a well-known Jazz &blues with the specially sorrow missing in love... as a romanticism piece...

Following Goldsmiths' Jazz standards, I re-edited it into piano, especially the running of major or minor seventh arpeggios (including flatten 5th and flatten 9th, sometimes) ... in left hand, its rhythm and matching way with melodic right hand... Meanwhile, I gave pedalling to bass for making a play-along effect and somehow, polyphonic layers...

I like this piano task- its tune, though didn't know the particular 'you' is whom... Two people's fates were twinning and weaving each other, like two trees... like my left hand and right hand... So luck... If it's Cole Porter... let us give him a best wish...

Hopefully, you enjoy my edition... have a hear? Thanks!

Artist.value: Jason M. C., Han

81111479.title: File:Listen to Mother's Old Story - Piano Pupil Yiwen, Cui.ogg

ImageDescription.value:
Yiwen, Cui (Direct translation of her Chinese name - A beautiful girl who is good at the translation of art and literature, from Cui family) is a quite and beautiful girl. To be honest, piano is a hard-job for her, but she and her family are insisted in it very much. She got a good life effect from this Chinese piano-kid's song - 'Listen to Mother's Old Story': making her family and parents happy, getting some confidences through this piano song from the examination, showing her fashion in my library concert held for piano kids...  After those more above, frequent exercises, and getting her permission, I can submit this classroom-recording edition. Though in the tail I found a note lost... and some parts of her left hand might run much more fluently... , I think her emotional background of this music reached to a good level, and those polyphonic parts can be clearly heard two layers, their cannoning, and so on... 
Congratulation! Hopefully, in future, you can understand this Chinese beautiful pentatonic piano-song in a better way.

Artist.value: Jason M. C., Han

81097371.title: File:Outing- Chinese kids' Piano Song - Junjun's edition (selected from real piano lesson).ogg

ImageDescription.value:
This sound-file was a real classroom recording of my and Ms Song's (my mother's) piano pupil - Junjun 's version of 'Outing' in the music textbook of Chinese National Grading Test. After getting the permission of him and his mother in the educational privacy, I can submit his good version. Junjun was only a 6-years-old boy, with his full name - Xi Jun, Zhou (Direct Chinese translation: A handsome boy from an excellent family who is good at intelligently thinking).

That's quite right that Junjun was a quite little (only 6), clever and handsome boy, with a pair of little & soft hands playing on the keyboard. When taking a seat for piano-playing, he evenly cannot touch the pedals by his own feet. However, after knowing that we would hold a non-profit library piano concert for kids and after his examination we would select some good versions to Wikimedia Commons and Wikiversity, He and his mother began to work hard in learning and practising. Times after times, we can hear a very clear & beautiful melodical river flowing in his 'piano outing time' out; meanwhile, not only the 'Mach-accompaniment' of his left hand and also in the polyphonic B (Double melodical following - in this small ABA form dancing song), he really did a good job in the hands-controlability. I can almost hear a 'Rit. - A Tempo' in minutes 0.24-0.29, which shows this boy was reveling in some beatiful landscapes alongside his outing river. Congratulation!

Yes, there must be some problems, such as.. in 0.55 minutes, the chord-grasping distributed into more than one sound...which shows a relatively weak hands' coordination at that moment... However, no one was in his or her obserlute perfection. To an 8-years-old boy, it has already been a hard-working and excellent performance. Hopefully, the growth of his piano performance would bring the happiness to his family. Thanks again. Let us listen to him!

Artist.value: Jason M. C., Han
